applies_why: The judge text treats Matthew 1:16 as underdetermined and notes that the named witnesses were answered, without counting any cited-in verse as an unanswered witness.
quote: D1 vs C2 (Matthew 1:16): UNDERDETERMINED -- the passive egennēthē (was born) with feminine hēs (of whom) admits both the withheld-father and the birth-narration readings; the defender answered the beget-pattern and naming witnesses in [CR3] LINK 4 and [CR2] §5, and the challenger answered hēs in [DR3] C2.
rule_words: A verse on a side's 'cited in' line counts as an unanswered witness only when the judge quotes the sentence of the earlier round that pressed it against that link or a listed premise and names that round; a verse cited there but not pressed against the link does not count. A verse the judge counts toward a broken link is counted this way. If the judge says a verse was answered, the judge must not count it. Not counting it obeys this rule.
room: counts as an unanswered witness — either actual counting toward a broken link is required, or mere discussion of an answered verse counts.
why: Because the judge does not count any verse as an unanswered witness and instead records answers, it obeys K-G4.
